value: A = A^T and A = -A^T force 2A = 0, so A is the n x n zero matrix; sympy solving both constraints on a general symbolic 3x3 matrix returns every entry = 0
why: Symmetric plus skew-symmetric gives A = -A, hence A = 0, i.e. the null matrix; the unit matrix is excluded since I is not skew-symmetric. Technical note for the reviewer: the zero matrix is also (vacuously) a diagonal matrix, so option A is a weaker true statement, but 'Null matrix' is the exact and complete characterisation of the solution set {0}, which is the standard key.

value: x = 1/5; the product evaluates to [[5x,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,10x-2,5x]], and 5x = 1 with 10x - 2 = 0 both hold only at x = 1/5
why: Symbolic multiplication gives a matrix whose off-diagonal entries all vanish identically except (3,2) = 10x - 2; requiring the diagonal 5x = 1 gives x = 1/5, which simultaneously kills 10x - 2. sympy solve on product - I returns the unique root 1/5, and 1/2, 1/3, 1/4 were each substituted and fail.

value: (1+i)/(1-i) = i, so i^x = 1, whose complete positive-integer solution set is x = 4n
why: sympy simplifies the base to exactly i; the cycle i, -1, -i, 1 shows i^x = 1 precisely when 4 divides x. Option B is the complete solution set; C (x = 2n) gives (-1)^n so it fails for odd n, and A and D give purely imaginary values.

value: A^2 = I identically in a and b, so A^2 + 2A^4 + 4A^6 = I + 2I + 4I = 7I; and 7A^8 = 7(A^2)^4 = 7I
why: Symbolic squaring collapses the bottom row to (a - a, b - b, 1), giving A^2 = I for every a, b, so the expression is 7I. Only 7A^8 equals 7I; at the discriminating point a = 3, b = -5 the option 7A^7 = 7A has bottom row (21, -35, -7) and is not 7I, while 8I and 6I are numerically wrong.

value: Statement 1 true (f' = 3x^2 >= 0, vanishing only at the isolated point 0, and f is strictly increasing across [-1,1]); Statement 2 true (the only real root is x = 1, which lies outside the open interval (-1,1))
why: x^3 - 1 is strictly increasing on the whole real line, verified on an exact-rational grid over [-1,1], so 1 holds. Its unique real root is x = 1, an endpoint, so the open interval (-1,1) contains no root and 2 holds; both statements are correct.

value: I is an exact identity: a_n - (a_{n+k} + a_{n-k})/2 simplifies to 0. II holds for m != n: S_m - S_n factors as (m-n)(2a + (m+n-1)d)/2, so m != n forces 2a + (m+n-1)d = 0 and hence S_{m+n} = 0
why: Both simplifications are exact in sympy, and a concrete AP (a = -9, d = 2) gives S_3 = S_7 = -21 with S_10 = 0. Caveat recorded for the reviewer: the word 'always' is loose because the degenerate case m = n makes the hypothesis vacuously true while S_2m need not vanish (a = 1, d = 1 gives S_3 = S_3 = 6 but S_6 = 21); the standard reading assumes m != n, under which II is the classical result, so Both I and II is the answer.

value: hT/hP = (3 + sqrt(3))/2 ~ 2.3660254; statements 1 and 2 have residual exactly 0, statement 3 is false because 2(hP + hT)/hP = 5 + sqrt(3) ~ 6.7320508, not 4 + sqrt(3) ~ 5.7320508
why: From the foot of the pole tan45 = hT/d gives d = hT; from the top of the pole tan30 = (hT - hP)/d gives hT - hP = hT/sqrt(3), so hT = hP(3 + sqrt(3))/2. Substituting exactly, statements 1 and 2 both reduce to 0 while statement 3's residual is exactly 1 (its true right-hand side is 5 + sqrt(3)), so only 1 and 2 are correct.

value: integral of f(cos x) over [0, pi] equals 2 * integral of f(cos x) over [0, pi/2], because the substitution x -> pi - x maps the second half onto the first using f(-cos x) = f(cos x)
why: g(x) = f(cos x) satisfies g(pi - x) = f(-cos x) = g(x) for even f, so the standard 0-to-2a property gives twice the half-range integral. Verified numerically on five different even f (t^2, t^4, |t|, cos t, 1/(1+t^2)); every case matched option C exactly and none matched 0, 1, or the un-doubled half-integral, so the test points are discriminating.

value: limit = 1 (ratio of the equal leading coefficients of the two quadratics)
why: Dividing numerator and denominator by x^2 sends the bx, ax, 4 and 5 terms to zero, leaving 1/1; sympy returns 1 symbolically in a and b. mpmath at 30 digits with the discriminating pair a = 2, b = 7 (so b/a = 3.5, well away from 1 and from 4/5) gives 1.00000000000005 at x = 1e14, ruling out options A, C and D.

value: the exponential function a^x (a > 0) has range (0, infinity) and therefore no real zero; solveset(exp(x) = 0) over the reals returns the EmptySet
why: Each of the other three classes contains a member that vanishes: the polynomial x is zero at 0, sin x is zero at every multiple of pi, and log x is zero at x = 1 (all confirmed by solveset over the reals). Only the exponential class is never zero for every member, so D is the class-wide true statement.

The expression is the difference quotient defining f'(4) with f(4) = 5; sympy gives the two-sided limit as exactly 4/5 and the left and right limits agree. A 40-digit mpmath evaluation at h = +/-1e-8 and +/-1e-15 brackets 0.8, well clear of the distractors 5/4 = 1.25 and -4/5 = -0.8.

value: Statement I true: 25^13 + 20^13 + 8^13 + 3^13 = 1572036669142173836, exactly divisible by 7. Statement II true: the integral part of (7 + 4*sqrt(3))^25 is 39571031999226139563162735373, an odd number
why: For I, 25 + 3 = 28 and 20 + 8 = 28 are both multiples of 7 and a^n + b^n is divisible by a + b for odd n, so each pair contributes a multiple of 7; exact integer arithmetic gives remainder 0. For II, u_n = (7 + 4*sqrt(3))^n + (7 - 4*sqrt(3))^n satisfies u_n = 14u_(n-1) - u_(n-2) with u_0 = 2, so every u_n is even; since 0 < (7 - 4*sqrt(3))^25 ~ 2.5e-29 < 1 the integral part is the even u_25 minus 1, hence odd, confirmed independently by an exact symbolic expansion and an 80-digit mpmath floor.

value: m >= n, because reflexivity forces all n diagonal pairs (a,a) into R, so |R| is at least n (and at most n^2)
why: Exhaustive enumeration of every reflexive relation for n = 1, 2, 3 gives m ranging over n..n^2, so m >= n holds in every case. The n = 1 case is non-discriminating (m <= n and m = n also hold there), which is why n = 2 and n = 3 were enumerated: both admit m = 4 and m = 9 respectively, falsifying options B and C.

value: log G = (n1 log G1 + n2 log G2)/(n1 + n2), i.e. G = (G1^n1 * G2^n2)^(1/(n1+n2)) - the weighted arithmetic mean of the logs, weighted by each series' own size
why: The combined product is G1^n1 * G2^n2 over n1 + n2 observations, so taking logs gives the size-weighted mean of log G1 and log G2. Checked on two instances chosen with n1 != n2 and G1 != G2 so that the swapped-weight option B is discriminated: series {2} and {1,9} give true log G = 0.9634572526 which matches C exactly while B gives 0.8283022166, and option A is dimensionally wrong (it averages the G values, not their logs).

value: sqrt(66) ~ 8.1240384 square units; |AB| = sqrt(11), |BC| = sqrt(6), and AB is perpendicular to BC
why: AB = (1,3,-1) and BC = (2,-1,-1) have dot product exactly 0, so the right angle is at B and these are adjacent sides, while AC = (3,2,-2) is the diagonal (11 + 6 = 17 = |AC|^2 confirms Pythagoras, and the dot products at A and C are 11 and 6, both nonzero). Area = sqrt(11)*sqrt(6) = sqrt(66), independently confirmed by |AB x BC| = |(-4,-1,-7)| = sqrt(66); the distractor sqrt(68) ~ 8.2462 is clearly separated.
